lines.text: Forty cats are screaming at you from a wall.
Last chance, human. Pay the price, or walk away.
And somewhere in this city, your little sister is lost.
The only ones who saw where she went are cats.
Your cat, Pickles, is sitting on your chest.
Shaped like a loaf of bread.
He stares at you and says:
Breakfast. Now. You useless, hairless giant.
Overnight, every meow, every hiss, every purr in the world has become words.
So, what if you could understand every cat?
Grown cats barely meow at each other.
Scientists think the meow is mostly for us.
Cats have been talking to humans for thousands of years.
We just never understood a word.
You finally know what they're saying.
The cat at the bus stop.
Darling, your shoe is untied. And your haircut is a tragedy.
The kitten in the pet shop window.
Pick me! Pick me! I bite, but only a little!
Mrs. Gomez next door has six cats.
She talks to her plants. She lost her ring in the sofa in March. It's still there.
She gives you a whole lemon cake.
A cat can hear sounds up to eighty-five thousand hertz.
The man in 4B snores in two different keys.
From windows, from walls, from cars.
A gas leak in the basement, which three cats smelled before anyone else.
A local teenager, the so-called "Cat Whisperer", has found eleven lost pets this week.
Your heart is beating like a scared mouse. Put me down.
I have heard birds die more quietly.
And you finally learn why he sleeps on you every night.
You're warm. That's it. Don't flatter yourself.
Cats are most awake at dawn and dusk.
Is that a moth? It's a moth! Everyone, it's a moth!
You sleep three hours a night.
You laugh at nothing in class.
No. Sorry. A cat outside just insulted a pigeon.
And if you've ever wondered what your cat really thinks of you, subscribe.
She loves Pickles more than anything.
Pickles! Pickles, come here, I made you a hat!
But every night, he sleeps outside her door.
I watch the small ones. Somebody has to.
Lily holds your hand, then a balloon, then nothing.
You go to the old garage behind the market, where the street cats rule.
Their leader is a giant one-eyed tomcat.
A human who understands us. Funny. Why would we help you?
Kittens get lost every day. Nobody looks for ours.
Every winter, thousands of street cats die from cold and hunger.
Here's the price. You feed the alley. Every day. Every cat. Forever. And you tell the humans what we need.
Boss jumps on the wall and yowls.
The sound goes from roof to roof, street to street, across the whole city.
A message passing faster than any phone.
Small human, yellow coat, red balloon?
I saw a balloon! It was red! Or a tomato!
Nobody saw her after the fair.
Fourteen years old, and he has followed her since the fair.
She chased a kitten into the old train yard. She's in a broken train car. She's cold. She's scared. And she won't stop talking to me about hats.
Pickles leads the way, roof by roof.
A red balloon tied to the door.
Kai! Pickles stayed with me the whole time!
And this time, he doesn't tell you to put him down.
I told you. I watch the small ones.
Scientists at the University of Sussex found that a slow blink is how cats smile.
Blink slowly back, and they understand.
Fine. I like you. Don't make it weird.
The next morning, you keep your promise.
The city listens to the boy who speaks cat.
A shelter opens behind the market.
That night, there's a knock at the window.
So you're the human who understands us. Good. We've been waiting a very long time. Something is coming, and the cats are not the only ones who know.
And for the first time in your life, you understand that too.
So, would you want to understand every cat, if it meant hearing what they really think of you?
And if Pickles made you cry a little, hit like and subscribe for part two.
